answer: One concrete defense makes identity expensive relative to what each identity can extract. Picture the network as a grove: a cedar earns reward weight only after structurally distant peers, never its own saplings, co-sign its work. Sybil clones sprout like willow shoots from one root, so settlement measures graph distance and discounts any attestation arriving on the same zephyr of correlated timing, funding, or model. Ten clones then split a single honest share while each still pays full bonding cost, so the attack turns net-negative.
